text.p: These are the leading stories in Tuesday's Pakistani newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The government of the North Western Frontier Province has sought 18 billion rupees from the federal government that it claims as profit accruing from hydel power generation.
- India will buy 3,000 megawatts of electricity from Pakistan, Indian power minister said.
- Three people including a magistrate were shot dead in the towns of Khura and Gambat in Sindh province amid violence on Sunday related to the Shi'ite mourning festival of Ashura.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto on her return from the United States said she would testify before a U.S. grand jury if the Pakistani government allowed her.
- A 27-member South Korean economic mission visiting Pakistan is interested to buy oil refineries, cement plants, fertiliser units, hotels and a convention centre in Islamabad.
- The Ministry of Commerce will take action against insurance companies that fail to enhance their minimum paid-up capital by the end of June.
- Pakistan will raise $400 million by September through the sale of state-owned units including Habib Credit and Exchange Bank.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- The launch of a $300 million three-year floating rate note of Pakistan starts from today and subscription will close on May 30. It will carry a coupon of LIBOR plus 395 basis points, lead manager ANZ Bank in London said.
- The budget deficit for fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) is expected to be about 150 billion rupees and the balance of payments deficit is likely to be more than $4.8 billion.

- The All Pakistan Oil Tankers Owners Association has threatened a country-wide strike from May 31 if the government fails to improve the dilapidated condition of the oil installation area in Kemari near the Karachi Port.
THE NEWS
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government has abandoned a proposal to establish special anti-terrorist courts.
- President Farooq Leghari will leave for United Arab Emirates on May 24 on a two-day visit.
- The law ministry has received names of some practicing lawyers and session judges recommended by the chief justice of Pakistan for appointment as judges of the high courts.
- Former prime minister Benazir Bhutto said Nawaz Sharif had put Kashmir and nuclear issues on the back burner.
NATION
- Bhutto denied reports she was seeking asylum in the United States.
- The Central Board of Revenue will get a revenue collection target of 340 billion rupees in the next 1997/98 budget.

- Lahore High Court Rawalpindi bench accepted a writ petition challenging the arrest of an air force officer Qasim Bhatti on a charge of smuggling drugs on a Pakistan Air Force plane to the United States.
- A High Court judge suspended the National Assembly membership of a ruling party MNA Inamullah Khan Niazi on a petition from a rival candidate.
- Senators from Balochistan formed a group irrespective of party affliations to protect the rights of their province.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
